svg.title: Four steps for one message
svg.desc: The four steps Graphiti runs for one message, traced with the first message of session 2. Step 1, an LLM call, finds three entities: Anton, pescatarian diet and peanut allergy. Step 2 matches them to stored entities: Anton and peanut allergy by exact name, with no call; pescatarian diet has no exact match, its name scores 0.691 against the stored 'vegetarian', above the 0.6 floor, so an LLM call is asked and says they are different: a new entity. Step 3, an LLM call, extracts two facts with dates: Anton started following a pescatarian diet about a month ago, replacing his previous vegetarian diet, dated 20 July; and Anton has a severe, anaphylactic peanut allergy, dated 14 March. Step 4 compares each new fact with stored ones. For the diet, code finds no fact between the same two entities and seven by search; an LLM call says it contradicts 'Anton has been strictly vegetarian for eight years'; code ends that fact on 20 July, because it started earlier. For the allergy, code finds the stored allergy fact between the same two entities; an LLM call says it is a duplicate, so nothing new is stored. In all: five LLM calls and three embedding calls; one fact added and one closed.
svg.text: Every message goes through the same four steps, one message at a time and in order. Here they are for the message that
changes a fact. The model makes judgements; plain code decides what is stored and when a fact ends.
“Small update on the food thing — I started eating fish about a month ago. So I'm pescatarian now, not vegetarian. Still no meat, and
the peanut situation obviously hasn't changed.”
In: the message, the ten messages before it, and the entity types. Out: the things it mentions.
0.691, over 0.6, so the model is asked
→ a different thing: a new node
In: the message and the entities. Out: facts between two of them, each a sentence with the date it
“Anton started following a pescatarian diet about a month ago, replacing his previous vegetarian
“Anton has a severe, anaphylactic peanut allergy.”
· between the same two entities: none
· by a search for its sentence: 7 stored facts
· the model: it contradicts “Anton has been strictly vegetarian for eight years”
· code: that fact started earlier (14 March), so it ends when this one starts, on 20 July. The
· between the same two entities: “Anton has a severe anaphylactic peanut allergy”
· the model: a duplicate of it
· nothing new is stored; the old fact keeps its dates
5 LLM calls (1 + 1 + 1 + 2) and 3 embedding calls. One fact added, one closed, one recognised as a repeat.
